name: Tomato
notes:
Tomatoes, nutrition from USDA. World yield ~38 t/ha (FAO). The US is ~97 t/ha, mostly California processing tomatoes. Water is Mekonnen & Hoekstra (lower in the US).

Emissions are Poore & Nemecek's tomato value (2.09 kg CO2e/kg), high for a vegetable. That average includes heated greenhouse tomatoes; field tomatoes alone are about 0.7. Many tomatoes you buy in winter are greenhouse-grown, so the higher figure is realistic for them.

Per-hectare erosion, pesticide (~3.5 kg/ha), fertilizer, tillage and CO2-capture values are older estimates whose notes don't explain their derivation.
land_types_note: Irrigated California and Mediterranean, plus China and India.

name: Potato
notes:
Potatoes, nutrition from USDA. World yield ~22 t/ha (FAO). The US gets ~50 t/ha (USDA NASS 2019–2023), so US potatoes need less than half the land per kg. Water is Mekonnen & Hoekstra; the US value is higher because of grey water from fertilizer runoff.

The per-hectare erosion, pesticide, fertilizer, tillage and CO2-capture values are older estimates whose notes cite the yield source rather than explaining the number.
land_types_note: China, Europe and Russia cropland, plus North American prairie.

name: Cassava
notes:
Cassava (manioc), a staple for hundreds of millions of people in Africa, Asia and Latin America. Nutrition is USDA raw cassava. It must be cooked to remove natural cyanide compounds, but boiling changes its weight little. 84% is edible.

Yield is FAOSTAT world (~10 t/ha). Water is Mekonnen & Hoekstra: almost all rain-fed, no irrigation. Emissions are Poore & Nemecek's cassava value (1.32 kg CO2e/kg), higher than other roots because of land-use change in the tropics.

There's no cassava pesticide or fertilizer data, so those are borrowed from sweet potato (another low-input tropical root crop; confidence 2). Before 2026-10-01 this data was missing, and the scorer counted it as zero pesticide deaths. That pushed cassava above corn in the rankings, which was wrong.
land_types_note: Grown across the humid and sub-humid tropics: Nigeria, DR Congo, Ghana and Tanzania (savanna and cleared forest), plus Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil.
